$comment: KluCode design tokens — the single source of truth. The website's tailwind.config.ts imports this file directly, so a change here reaches the site with no copy-paste step. Contrast ratios in `wcag` were computed against paper (#F2F4F1) and ink (#0C1A15); see 03-visual-identity.md for the rules they imply.

viridian.$comment: Generated by build_palette.py in OKLCH — do not hand-edit. Even perceptual lightness ladder, chroma peaking at 500/600 and tapering at both ends, and deliberate hue torsion (cooler tints, deeper shades). 500 is THE brand colour and is display-only: it fails AA for body text on both paper and ink.

stone.$comment: Generated by build_palette.py. Near-neutral by design: chroma 0.004-0.010, an order of magnitude below the old hand-picked scale, with the hue held steady instead of drifting 34 degrees. The neutrals must be somewhere the eye can rest, or the whole page reads as one muddy hue. 50 is paper, 950 is ink.

semantic.$comment: Interface states only — form validation, status pills, alert boxes. These are NOT brand colours and never appear in marketing material or the logo. warningSurface is the one warm value left in the system, and it is confined to alert boxes on purpose: an alert that is not warm does not read as an alert.

glass.$comment: NAVIGATION LAYER ONLY. This used to dress ~27 elements per screen as 'clear glass'; measured, it was doing nothing. A 0.10 white fill with no border over a near-white page composited to 1.007:1 against that page — the cards had no edge at all in light mode — and both the 6px blur and the SVG displacement rim are no-ops over a smooth gradient, which is all that was ever behind them. Everything that carried content moved to the flat `.panel` material, which builds elevation out of surfaceRaised + border instead of faking it out of translucency. What survives is the sticky header capsule, the one element with real page content moving underneath it, which is also the only place Apple's own guidance puts this material. `fill` is deliberately high (0.86, was 0.10): the capsule passes over the ink footer as you scroll, and at a low fill the nav labels composite below AA against it. 0.86 is the measured floor — check_contrast.py composites every nav text role over the darkest and lightest backdrops the capsule can cross and fails the build below 4.5:1. lensBand/lensScale/fillStrong/edge/depth are gone with the lens and the variants that used them.

role.$comment: Two designed themes, not one theme and its inversion. Light builds hierarchy by going DARKER as elements recede; dark builds it by going LIGHTER as elements are raised, which is how physical light works and what dark mode actually needs. Dark also uses off-white text rather than pure white, and moves the accent UP the scale where the chroma taper has already softened it — saturated colour on a dark ground vibrates. Dark muted text sits at stone.300, not 400: measured against the header capsule over a lit area, 400 came out at 4.31:1 — below AA. Dark grounds eat contrast that light grounds do not. The ink* roles are the closing slab at the foot of the page. They are deliberately NOT surfaceInverse: inverting the surface makes the footer follow the theme in the wrong direction, so dark mode ended up with a white footer glued to the bottom of a dark page. The footer is dark by design in both themes — in dark mode it lifts to stone.900 rather than inverting, which is the same raised-is-lighter rule the rest of dark mode follows.

display.$comment: Headlines and the wordmark. Geometric grotesque with enough character to be recognisable at a glance.

body.$comment: Everything readable. Chosen for its German-language diacritics and long-text legibility.

mono.$comment: Eyebrow labels, tags, technical detail. The signal that says 'a developer built this'. Never body copy.

scale.$comment: Type scale, fluid between a 360px and a 1280px viewport.

space.$comment: 4px base grid. Section rhythm is deliberately generous — whitespace is the brand.

radius.$comment: Restrained. The logo's node circles supply the roundness; boxes stay close to square.

motion.$comment: Motion is functional, never decorative. Everything must be wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion.
